skill.name: youtube-comments-api-skill
skill.description: Extract YouTube video metadata and public comment data through the BrowserAct YouTube Comments API workflow.
skill.summary: Run a BrowserAct workflow to collect YouTube search results and public comments for research.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or malware intent was found in the reviewed files. The skill performs its stated BrowserAct workflow, but it executes a local Python helper, sends data to a third-party API, and includes risky guidance for users to provide an API key in chat.

remediation.suggestion: Require BROWSERACT_API_KEY from an environment variable or secret manager, and remove instructions that ask users to paste keys into chat.
Document the BrowserAct API endpoint, transmitted fields, retention expectations, and require user consent before running the workflow.
Validate comments_limit and scroll_count as bounded integers before sending them to the API to reduce cost and abuse risk.
Add guidance for privacy review, data minimization, and compliance with YouTube terms before collecting or storing commenter data.

content.value_statement: Manual YouTube comment collection is slow and inconsistent. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow to return video metadata and public comments from search keywords.
actual_capabilities: Runs a bundled Python script that starts a BrowserAct YouTube Comments workflow.
Accepts search keywords, per-video comment limits, and comment scroll counts.
Polls BrowserAct task status until completion or timeout.
Returns video titles, URLs, publication times, and view counts when available.
Returns public comment text, commenter details, likes, publish dates, and reply counts.
Handles missing or invalid BrowserAct API key errors with user-facing messages.
limitations: Requires a valid BrowserAct API key configured before use.
Sends search parameters and authentication data to BrowserAct services.
Can time out after several minutes if the external workflow is slow.
Only retrieves data exposed by the BrowserAct template and YouTube public pages.

use_cases.title: Research Audience Reactions
use_cases.description: Collect public comments for a topic and summarize themes, objections, and frequent questions.

use_cases.title: Compare Competitor Videos
use_cases.description: Gather search result metadata and viewer comments around competing products or creators.

use_cases.title: Track Topic Sentiment
use_cases.description: Monitor comments for recurring sentiment signals around launches, events, or trending keywords.

prompt_templates.title: Collect Basic Comments
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small comment sample.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the YouTube comments skill to search for "AI productivity tools". Collect up to 10 comments per video with 2 scrolls, then summarize the main themes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Topics
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate research across related keyword sets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the skill for "Claude Code tutorial" and "Codex tutorial" with 15 comments per video. Compare viewer questions, praise, and pain points.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Sentiment Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured analysis for a research report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search YouTube for "browser automation API" and collect comments with 20 comments per video. Group the results by positive, negative, and neutral sentiment.

prompt_templates.title: Build Competitive Insight
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for product and marketing teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill on three competitor keyword phrases. Extract video metadata, identify repeated feature requests, and create a prioritized insight brief.

output_examples.input: Search for "AI note taking apps" with 10 comments per video.
output_examples.output: A concise report lists matching videos, public comment themes, common complaints, and notable engagement signals.

output_examples.input: Collect comments for "robot vacuum review" and summarize purchase concerns.
output_examples.output: The response highlights repeated concerns such as battery life, mapping accuracy, price, support, and replacement parts.

output_examples.input: Compare YouTube comments for two product launch keywords.
output_examples.output: The output contrasts audience sentiment, recurring questions, and high-interest topics for each launch keyword.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY through a secure environment variable before running the skill.
Use small comment and scroll limits first to control cost and review data quality.
Review YouTube terms, privacy duties, and retention rules before storing comment data.
anti_patterns: Do not paste BrowserAct API keys into shared chats or reports.
Do not collect more public commenter data than the research task requires.
Do not treat public YouTube comments as representative survey data without sampling context.

faq.question: What does this skill need to run?
faq.answer: It needs Python, the bundled script, network access, and a valid BROWSERACT_API_KEY.

faq.question: Does it scrape YouTube directly from my browser?
faq.answer: No. It calls a BrowserAct workflow that performs the YouTube comment collection task.

faq.question: What data can it return?
faq.answer: It can return video metadata and public comment fields such as text, author display name, likes, and reply counts.

faq.question: Can it analyze sentiment by itself?
faq.answer: It collects the raw comment data. The agent can then summarize themes or classify sentiment from the returned results.

faq.question: Is an API key optional?
faq.answer: No. The BrowserAct API key is required, and it should be supplied through a secure environment variable.

faq.question: What should I check before using the data?
faq.answer: Check YouTube terms, privacy obligations, sample size, and whether storing commenter information is necessary.
